Commentary.Commentary: As mentioned earlier, it's a challenging total and South Africa will have to bat sensibly to overhaul it. They bat deep which is an advantage and also the ground is on the smaller side. New Zealand, too, will have to be right on the money in the field. Promises to be an intriguing battle. Join us in a short while.

South Africa bowled well but will not be pleased with the way the innings ended. They conceded too many runs in the death overs and looked a bit clueless. Chris Morris was the standout performer, claiming a 4-fer but his last two overs went for 38 runs which spoiled his figures. Kagiso Rabada did an excellent job, while Imran Tahir and Tabraiz Shamsi also were decent in their respective spells.

Jimmy Neesham and Mitchell Santner steadied the innings with a decent partnership and then the pair of Colin de Grandhomme and Tim Southee added a quickfire 51-run stand off only 23 balls to take the Kiwi total past the 200-run mark.

What a finish by New Zealand! They hammered 61 runs in the last five overs and have posted a challenging total on the board. After a steady start, the home team lost wickets in a flurry to find themselves in a spot of bother. Kane Williamson, however, looked in fine touch and notched up his 28th ODI fifty to keep the Kiwi innings going. His wicket was a big blow to New Zealand but the lower order stepped up to the plate.

FOUR! Angling into the stumps, Southee gets his front foot out of the way and smacks it over the mid-wicket region for a boundary. 25 off the last over and 50-run stand comes up as well. NEW ZEALAND END ON 207/7!
SIX! When he hits, it stays hit! Fuller delivery outside off, Southee has smashed that over the wide long on region for a biggie. This guy comes and makes a mark whenever required.
FOUR! Short delivery into the body, Southee top edges his attempted pull shot over the keeper's head for a boundary. Lucky runs.

FOUR! TOP SHOT! Length delivery outside off, Southee gets behind the line of the ball and slaps it through covers. The fielder at sweeper cover goes to his right and tries to cut it off with a dive but the ball wins the race.
Fuller delivery outside off, Colin drives it straight towards the fielder at covers for a quick single.
SIX! Full toss on the pads, Colin de Grandhomme flicks it off his pads for a biggie over the fine leg region. Great shot! That's actually a freebie to start the over.
The batsman has driven it through mid off. One run added to the total.
On the pads, Colin clips it through the square leg region for a couple.
SIX! Length delivery outside off, Colin smells the width and hoists it over the point region for a biggie. Top shot!
Again a slower delivery, Colin goes for a pull but misses.
Bye! Slower delivery outside off, Southee is beaten by it and the ball goes straight to the keeper. Colin calls him for a single. Quinton has a shy at the striker's end but misses.

On the pads, Colin clips it towards mid-wicket and goes for a quick single. The fielder has a shy at the non-striker's end but he misses this time. A direct hit would have Colin de Grandhomme back in the hut.

NOT OUT! Angling into the pads, Southee clips it towards mid-wicket and goes for a single. The fielder has a shy at the non-striker's end and he hits. The ball ricochets and the batsmen manage to pick up another run in the process. The fielders however appeal for a run out and it's referred upstairs. The replays show that Southee was just in.
Run out appeal is referred upstairs...

In the air.... Safe! Fuller delivery outside off, Southee gets under it as he lofts it towards mid on. The fielder from long on comes and tries to catch it but it falls way short of him. They manage to run a couple.
Short delivery into the body, Southee goes for a pull but misses it completely.
Good length delivery outside off, de Grandhomme swings his bat at it but gets an inside edge onto his pads. The ball tickles away on the off side and the batsmen run a single.
Full toss on the pads, Colin flicks it through backward square leg. They pick up a couple in the process.
SIX! TOP SHOT! Good length delivery outside off, Colin de Grandhomme stays deep in his crease and swings hard at it. The ball goes just over the fielder at long on for a biggie
Chris Morris is back for a bowl.
The batsman tries hooking that one but misses it completely.
The batsman was beaten and missed the line of the delivery. Rabada toying with Tim.
Slower delivery outside off, Southee is foxed by it and ends up flashing and missing.

Terrific effort by Behardien! Nearly took a blinder! Once again it's a short of a length delivery outside off, Southee camps back and slaps it in the air over point. Behardien in the deep comes rushing across to his left and takes the catch with a dive. But the momentum keeps taking him near the ropes and Farhaan shows great alertness to release the ball before making contact with the fence. He tries to toss it towards the third man fielder who has come a bit close to him but it falls short of him. By the time the throw comes to the keeper, the batsmen have taken a couple of runs.
Short of a length around off, Southee stays back and taps it down to covers.
Tim Southee is in next.

OUT! Neesham falls! Rabada spears in a shortish ball, angling into the batsman and not rising much, Jimmy swivels with the pull shot but gets a top edge behind to the keeper. Quinton de Kock makes no mistake and Rabada strikes first ball of his new spell. That's a big wicket at this juncture of the game as Neesham is known for his power hitting.
Wide! Rabada runs in from around the wicket and sprays a length delivery wide outside off, Neesham leaves it and the umpire exercises his arms.
Kagiso Rabada is back on.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads. One run added to the total.
Colin drives it towards the fielder at long on for a single.

RUN OUT CHANCE MISSED! Tossed up outside off, de Grandhomme goes for a drive but he gets an outside edge which flies through the vacant slip region. The fielder from point gives it a chase and saves the boundary. The batsmen pick up two comfortably and go for the third. The chasing fielder throws at the keeper's end and de Kock is quick to realize that the non-striker is struggling to reach in time. He has a shy at the non-striker's end but he misses which results in an over throw. de Grandhomme calls for the fourth run and they manage to complete it comfortably.
Wrong 'un again, Colin goes for a heave but is beaten by the inward spin as it hits him on his box.
Short and wide outside off, Neesham punches it through covers for a single.
Wrong 'un pitched between middle and off, Neesham goes for a pull but gets a bottom edge as the ball sneaks past the keeper for a couple.
Imran Tahir is called back for a bowl.
Terrific delivery, nearly hits the blockhole, Colin goes hard at it and is lucky to get some bat on it. Digs it out somehow and it goes off the inside half past the stumps. Just 4 runs off the over!
Short ball on off, turning away, Neesham rocks back and smacks it to sweeper cover for one.
Walks down to the pitch of the ball and clips it a bit uppishly but wide of mid-wicket for a single.
Floated full ball on the pads, nudged through square leg for a run.
Flatter, shorter and quicker outside off, Neesham camps back to play the square cut but fails to connect.
Tossed up ball on middle, de Grandhomme goes back and turns it down to long leg for a run.
Tabraiz Shamsi comes back into the attack.
Fuller and on off, Neesham fails to get under this delivery and hits it back to the bowler.

Dropped by Behardien? Andile angles across a length ball on off, Neesham clears his front leg for a heave across the line but gets a fat top edge. The ball balloons in the air, Behardien rushes forward and across from the deep but fails to catch it as it drops just wide of his outstretched left hand. Two runs added to the total.
Back of a length delivery outside off, Neesham hangs back and pulls it past the mid-wicket fielder. Morris moves across to his right in the deep and stops the ball. Only two runs taken, poor running.
Lands it full and outside off, de Grandhomme drives it to wide mid off and scampers across to the other end.
A touch short and on off, it's pulled over mid-wicket for a run.
Angles across a length ball on off, Jimmy defends it down from the crease.
Andile Phehlukwayo to continue...
Powerplay 3 signalled. Maximum five fielders now allowed outside the ring.
Good length delivery outside off, de Grandhomme pushes it towards the cover region. No runs taken.
Angling into the pads, Colin clips it straight to the fielder at mid-wicket.
Colin de Grandhomme will replace Mitchell Santner in the middle.

OUT! Rabada comes around the wicket and digs it short this time. Santner goes for a hook but the ball gets big on him as it hits something on its way to the keeper. Quinton takes a fine catch over his head and starts appealing. The umpire is unmoved. De Kock convinces his skipper to go for the review and AB de Villiers acknowledges by going for it. Hot Spot shows that there was a top edge. The umpire has to change his decision and Santner has to walk back to the pavilion. South Africa have been successful with both their reviews today.
Appeal for a caught behind. The umpire remains unmoved. Quinton de Kock is confident of an edge and he convinces his skipper to go for the review.
Slower delivery on the pads, Santner tries to clip it but he misses as the ball hits him on the thigh pad.
TOP SAVE! Good length delivery outside off, Santner tries to cut it but he gets a bottom edge which goes towards the keeper. De Kock dives full stretch to his left and saves a certain boundary.
Short and angling into the stumps, Santner stays deep in his crease and tries to push it on the off side but he is beaten by the away movement.
FOUR! Down the leg side, Neesham flicks it elegantly through the square leg region for a boundary. Beautiful timing.
Again outside off, Santner slashes hard but straight to the fielder at third man for a single.
Wide outside off, Neesham guides it towards third man for a single.
Length delivery into the stumps, Santner prods forward in defense but he gets an inside edge onto his pads. The ball tickles towards the point region and the batsmen take a single.
Angling into the stumps, Santner stays in his crease and defends it on the off side.
Down the leg side, Neesham clips it towards short fine leg for a single.
Andile Phehlukwayo is back into the attack.
Santner stays in his crease and defends it.
Angling into the stumps, Neesham clips it through the mid-wicket region for a single.
Back of a length delivery outside off, Santner stays deep in his crease and dabs it towards point for a quick single.
FOUR! Fuller delivery outside off, Santner gets to the pitch of the ball and lofts it over the bowler's head for a boundary. That was a top shot.
Yorker on off, Santner digs it out.
Width on offer outside off, Neesham stays back and steers it through backward point for a single.
Kagiso Rabada is back into the attack.
Floated outside off, Santner lunges forward in defense and calls for a quick single. Neesham sends him back.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Wrong 'un this time, Santner reads it late as he defends it off the back foot.
Floated up in the line of the stumps, Neesham gets to the line of the ball and drives it straight down the ground for a single towards long on.
Short outside off again, Santner slaps it down the ground towards long on for a single.
Short in the line of the stumps, Santner pushes it straight to the fielder at covers.
Imran Tahir is called back for a bowl.
Punched off the back foot by the batsman. They pick up a single.

In the air....safe! Floated on the middle and leg, Neesham goes to clip it on the leg side but he is beaten by the away spin. The ball catches the leading edge and flies over the infield for a single. The sweeper cover fielder comes charging in but the ball falls in front of him.
Down the leg side, Santner clips it through the mid-wicket region for a single.
Floated outside off, Santner cuts it straight to the fielder at backward point.
Too wide outside off, Santner thinks of playing at it but changes his mind at the last moment as he hangs his bat in the air.
FOUR! PLACEMENT! Short and wide outside off, Santner slashes it past the diving point fielder. The cover fielder gives it a chase but the ball wins the race to the fence.
Outside off, Santner camps back and punches it through covers for a single.
Short into the stumps, Santner camps back and pulls it through the mid-wicket region for a couple.
Angling into the pads, Santner gets his front leg out of the way and pushes it back to the bowler.
Tossed up outside off, Santner drives it straight to the fielder at covers.
Fuller on the stumps, Santner lunges in defence but he gets an outside edge which goes towards point.
Short into the body, Neesham camps back and punches it towards long on for a single.
JP Duminy is introduced into the attack.
Flattish on off, Santner gets on the back foot and punches it to the off side.
Mitchell Santner walks out to bat.

OUT! DRAGS IT ON! Big blow to the Kiwis as their skipper departs. Tossed up outside off, Williamson goes for a cut but he is beaten by the inward spin. It catches the inside edge of his bat and rattles the stumps. Kane has to walk back after playing a fluent knock. Shamsi gets his first wicket of the match and he will like to add a few more to his tally.
FOUR! Floated outside off, Williamson gets to the pitch of the ball and drives it through the cover region for a boundary. Top shot!
FOUR! Short into the stumps, Williamson sweeps it hard through the square leg region for a boundary.
Floated up, Neesham drives it towards long off for a single.
Tossed up outside off and spinning away, Neesham camps back and tries to defend it but he is beaten by the away spin. That was a cracking delivery.
Tickles it off the inner half of the bat to fine leg for one.
Gets behind the line of the delivery and blocks.
Neesham has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
FOUR! Tahir is on the shorter side around off, turning away, Neesham plays a late cut and finds the third man fence.
Pushed to the cover region by the batsman. One run added to the total.
Spinning away, Williamson gets squared up a bit and defends it at the last moment.
Maiden! Tossed up and outside off, Neesham drags it across the line but finds the fielder on the leg side.
Lunges and brings his bat and pads together in defense.
Lets out a full toss this time, Neesham whips it across the line but the mid-wicket fielder makes a diving stop.
Fuller around off and it's forced back towards the bowler. Shamsi uses his boot to stop the ball.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Flatter and outside off, tapped down to point.
Down the leg side, Jimmy  has heaved it to deep square leg for a run.
Quicker through the air. Neesham pushes it towards mid-wicket.
28th ODI fifty for skipper Kane Williamson.
Floated up, Kane drives it down the ground towards long on for a single. The skipper is leading from the front.
Tossed up but full this time, Williamson clips it on the leg side but straight to the fielder at mid-wicket.
Fuller into the stumps, Williamson pushes it back to the bowler.
Down the leg side, Kane paddles it fine down the leg side. The batsmen manage to take a couple.
Imran Tahir is back into the attack. Spin from both ends now.
Flatter ball on off, defended off the back foot by Neesham.
An attempted googly around off, it's eased through mid off for a run.
SIX! Williamson continues to bat fluently. He goes down on one knee to a full ball around middle and off and slogs it over mid-wicket for a maximum.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Williamson pushes it towards mid on.

Tossed up on the leg stump and spinning into the pads, Williamson tries to clip it but he misses. The balls hits him on his pads. The players appeal but the umpire says no as it was going down the leg side.
Jimmy Neesham comes out to bat.

OUT! SOFT DISMISSAL! Short delivery into the body, Broom goes for a pull but fails to middle it. The ball flies of the top edge towards the fielder at square leg. Behardien takes a dolly as it comes straight to him. Morris is toying with the Kiwi batsmen. He has taken all the four wickets so far and is looking deadly.
Good length delivery outside off, Williamson dabs it on the off side for a quick single.
Fuller into the stumps, Broom just pushes it with soft hands towards mid on. They rush for a single and comfortably complete it.
Angling into the stumps, Williamson guides it towards third man for a single.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Dug in short into the body, Williamson sways away from the line of the delivery.
Beauty of a delivery! A googly by Shamsi, landing around off and squaring up the batsman completely, Broom is foxed, fails to put bat on ball and it goes off his back pad to first slip.
Shortish and on middle, turned through square leg for one.
FOUR! Nicely done! Loopy delivery, full and around leg, spinning a shade towards off, Williamson kneels and nails his sweep shot to deep backward square leg for a boundary.
Floated full ball on middle, Broom knocks it down to long on and gets off the mark with a run.
A slip in place for the new batsman.
Flighted delivery on middle, flicked in front of square leg for a single.
Flatter one on off, defended off the back foot.
Neil Broom is the next man in.

OUT! Morris has struck twice in this over! Fuller delivery angling into the stumps, Taylor pushes it straight to the bowler, more of a check shot as it stops a bit onto the batsman. Morris takes a fine return catch in his followthrough. The visitors have the upper hand in this contest after this sensational over by Morris.
Fuller on the stumps, Ross drives it straight to the fielder at mid on.
Angling into the stumps, Williamson stays deep in his crease as he gets cramped for room. The ball goes off an outside edge and travels fine on the off side. A single is taken.
A bit short into the body, Taylor just defends it on the leg side and he rushes for a single. The batsmen take on the fielder at mid-wicket and take a run.
On the pads, Williamson clips it through mid-wicket for a single.
Ross Taylor comes out to bat in the middle.

OUT! Brownlie holes out! Morris bangs in a short delivery around middle and invites the batsman to have a go. Dean takes the challenge of playing the pull shot but it comes off the upper half of the bat. The ball flies towards the fielder at deep mid-wicket where Behardien goes a bit towards his left and takes a well judged catch near the fence. Morris has taken a wicket of his very first delivery of the second spell.
Chris Morris is back into the attack.
50-run stand between Dean Brownlie and Kane Williamson.
Short down the leg side, Brownlie pulls it through mid-wicket for a single.
On the pads, Williamson flicks it towards deep square leg for a single.
Tossed up outside off and spinning in, Williamson camps back instead of going forward. Gets cramped for room but still manages to defend it.
Short and wide outside off, Dean camps back and punches it through the extra cover region for a single.
On the pads, Williamson this time sits and pulls it a bit wide but towards deep square leg for a single.
Short and spinning into the pads, Brownlie pulls it to deep square leg for a single.
Tabraiz Shamsi is brought into the attack.
On the pads, Brownlie clips it on the leg side for a single.
Williamson drives it towards long on for a single.

Chance? Tossed up around off, Williamson goes for a slog sweep but fails to keep it down. AB de Villiers tries to reach it with a dive at mid-wicket but it's too far from him. The ball goes in the deep as the batsmen run a couple.
A bit short and Brownlie camps back and pushes it towards long on for a single.
Again tossed up outside off, Kane drives it down the ground towards long off for a single.
Fuller delivery just outside off, Williamson lunges forward in defense.
Williamson plays it with an angled bat and guides it to third man. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Another short ball by Andile, this time Kane hooks it over mid-wicket and collects a couple of runs.
Wide called for height! Phehlukwayo digs in a short ball and it goes well over the head of the batsman.
Fullish and angling in, a hint of shape there, Williamson gets forward and defends it back solidly.
Turns a full length ball on the leg side but finds the fielder.
Slower delivery, on a length and outside off, 116 kph, Williamson hits it from the crease but fails to time and place it properly. Straight to mid on it goes.
Serves it on a fuller length around off, Kane brings down an angled bat after getting forward and pushes it towards backward point.
Short and wide outside off, Brownlie cuts it towards the fielder at point.
Fuller outside off, Williamson drives it towards long off for a single.
Down the leg side, Brownlie camps back and turns it around towards backward square leg for a single.
Fuller outside off, Williamson drives it through covers for a single.
SIX! OUT OF THE PARK! Floated up just outside off, Williamson sits down and slog sweeps it over the mid-wicket region. This one has gone the distance and Williamson looks in a really good touch.
Fuller delivery outside off, Williamson drives it straight to the fielder at covers.
Drops it full and outside off, Dean drives it off his front foot to mid off. 8 runs off the over!
Angles in a full ball on off, it's defended back.
Width on offer outside off, it's slashed through the line and the cover-point fielder dives to his left to take the pace off the ball. They take a couple of runs.
Gets behind the line of the delivery and blocks.
FOUR! Once again it's on the shorter side and the batsman places his pull shot better this time, far away from the left side of the deep mid-wicket fielder and fetches a boundary.
Short and pulled over mid-wicket for a couple of runs.
Again short this time, Brownlie camps back and pushes it down the ground for a single.
Short and wide outside off, Williamson goes back and punches it through the point region. Rabada gives it a chase and puts in a dive to save the boundary. The batsmen still manage to take three runs.
On the pads, Brownlie clips it through square leg for a single.
Brownlie gets to the pitch of the ball and defends it.
Floated outside off, Williamson goes for a punch through covers but he gets an outside edge which goes towards third man. A single is taken.
Tossed outside off, Williamson punches it towards the fielder at point.
Imran Tahir comes in for a bowl. Spin is introduced for the first time today.
Powerplay 2 begins. Maximum four fielders are allowed outside the circle.
On a length outside off, Williamson dabs it with soft hands towards point and takes a single.
Back of a length delivery, Williamson camps back and defends it.
Down the leg side, Brownlie clips it through the mid-wicket region for a single.
Fuller delivery into the stumps, Brownlie drives it towards mid off.
Length delivery outside off, Dean tries to cut it but he manages to find a bottom edge. The ball tickles away towards point.
Back of a length delivery into the body, Brownlie camps back and pushes it towards the fielder at mid on.
Andile Phehlukwayo is introduced into the attack.
Good length delivery outside off, Williamson pushes it towards mid off.
Angling into the pads, Dean flicks it towards fine leg. Shamsi cuts it off quickly and the batsmen pick up a single.

Again down the leg side, Williamson just clips it through the mid-wicket region. The fielder gives it a chase and stops the ball from going to the fence. They manage to pick up three runs in the process.
FOUR! CLASSY! On the pads, Williamson clips it through the square leg region elegantly for a boundary.
Williamson lunges forward and defends it.
That ball has struck the batsman on the thigh-pad.
Good length delivery outside off, Brownlie pushes it towards the fielder at point.
Brownlie camps back and defends it.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
On the pads, Williamson clips it down the leg side towards fine leg. One run is taken.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.
That ball has taken the inside edge onto the pads. The ball goes towards the square leg region and the batsmen manage to pick up a single.
Skipper Kane Williamson will bat at number 3.

OUT! Latham is gone! Morris pitches it in line of the stumps and gets it to swerve back in off the seam, Latham falls over to the off side in an attempt to flick it across the line but misses. He is rapped on the pads, they appeal but the umpire remains unmoved. The bowler, keeper and skipper have a chat and AB de Villiers takes a really late call to go for the DRS, in fact after the umpire has signaled it as the end of the over. The replays show that it's pitched in line, hit the pads in line and would have crashed into the stumps. Early success for the Proteas. However, the timing of the review will be a point of debate.
Appeal for an LBW is not upheld. AB de Villiers takes a really late call to take a review.
Length delivery outside off, left alone.
Down the leg side, DB clips it fine down the leg side to collect a single.
Angling into the pads, Brownlie stays deep in his crease and clips it towards mid-wicket.
FOUR! That's slapped! Good length delivery outside off, Brownlie finally makes use of the width as he slashes it over the point region for a boundary.
Fuller delivery just outside off, Brownlie drives it down the ground but straight to the fielder at mid on.
Fuller delivery angling into the stumps. Latham leans forward and defends it.
Yorker on the stumps, Latham digs it out and keeps it at bay. The ball tickles away towards point.
Good length delivery outside off, Latham tries to poke at it but he is beaten by the away movement.
Down the leg side, Latham tries to clip it fine but he misses. The ball hits him on the thigh pads.
WIDE! Rabada fails to pitch his short ball properly. Again digs it in short and that's over the head of the batsman. The umpire has signaled it as a wide.
Fuller delivery in the line of the stumps, Latham leans forward and defends it.
Good length delivery outside off, left alone.
Fuller delivery just outside off, Brownlie drives it straight to the fielder at covers.
FOUR! First boundary from the bat! Short into the body, Brownlie stays tall and smacks it through the mid-wicket region for a boundary. That was a top shot.
WIDE! Down the leg side, Brownlie goes to clip it but misses. Wide is signalled by the umpire.
Good length delivery outside off, Brownlie shuffles a bit and goes for a drive but is totally beaten by the away movement.
Similar delivery but this time he gets a bit of extra bounce. Dean misses it again as he goes to cut it.
Length delivery outside off, Brownlie slashes at it but misses. He fails to pounce on the width this time.
Good length delivery outside off, Brownlie pushes it straight to the fielder at covers.
Chris Morris will bowl with the second new ball from the other end.
Latham gets in line of the delivery and defends it.
Fuller delivery into the stumps, Tom drives it towards mid on.
Good length delivery outside off, Latham stays in his crease and defends it towards mid off.
FIVE WIDES! Dug in way short and too high. Latham sways away and the keeper cannot reach it as the ball goes over his head. Straight to the boundary.
Full toss on the stumps, Brownlie gets off the mark as he flicks it through mid-wicket for a triple. Easy pickings.
A touch short in length delivery just outside off, angling in, Brownlie shuffles a bit and flicks it towards mid-wicket.
PLAY AND A MISS! Totally no foot movement there to start with. Fuller delivery outside off, Brownlie goes for a drive but he is beaten by the away movement.

Right then, it's time to play the game. Dean Brownlie and Tom Latham are the Kiwi openers. It's going to be Kagiso Rabada to begin proceedings with the first new ball. Two slips in place. 6-3 field, very orthodox. Here we go...
South Africa - Hashim Amla, Quinton de Kock(w), Faf du Plessis, AB de Villiers(c), JP Duminy, Farhaan Behardien, Chris Morris, Andile Phehlukwayo, Kagiso Rabada, Imran Tahir, Tabraiz Shamsi.
New Zealand - Dean Brownlie, Tom Latham(w), Kane Williamson(c), Ross Taylor, Neil Broom, Jimmy Neesham, Mitchell Santner, Colin de Grandhomme, Tim Southee, Ish Sodhi, Trent Boult.

Toss - Up goes the coin, AB de Villiers calls it correctly and SOUTH AFRICA WILL FIELD! Kane Williamson was also looking to bowl first. Not a surprise, it's always better to chase in a rain-affected game.

Hello and a warm welcome everyone for the coverage of the first ODI between New Zealand and South Africa in Hamilton. Both sides will be raring to go and start the 5-match series on a positive note. The Proteas would look to build on the momentum after their excellent win in the last game. The home team on the other hand will be eyeing a comeback in this match. Stay tuned for toss...

Hurray! After a long delay, we finally are all set to get started. The match has been reduced to 34 overs per side owing to the time lost due to bad weather. Anyway, something is better than nothing. Powerplay overs - 1 to 7 (first PP), 8 to 27 (second PP) and 28 to 34 (third PP). Four bowlers can bowl maximum of 7 overs, while one can bowl six.
